info.description: A REST + WebRTC interface for managing live video, AI events, face authentication, and device configuration on a ViOnyx AI camera. JWT bearer auth, JSON request/response, OpenAPI 3.0.3. :::caution[Disclaimer · Legal Notice] This API is provided is subject to change. We reserve the right to modify, add, or remove any functionality, fields, or access permissions at our sole discretion. Users should be aware that any change, edit and update may occur and are encouraged to frequently review the API documentation for updates. We strive to minimize changes; however, we shall not be liable for any losses or damages arising from API modifications or discontinuation due to functional or specification changes. ::: :::note **AI CAM WebServer API · v1.0.0** Server URL: `https://{{your-vionyx-ip}}/v1/api` ::: --- ## Getting Started All requests use the `{{baseUrl}}` (default: `https://{{device-host}}/v1/api`) and `{{accessToken}}` collection variables. Set `device-host` to the target ViOnyx camera's IP address or hostname, and set `accessToken` to the `access_token` issued by `POST /auth/login`. This value is sent as a Bearer token through the collection-level Authorization setting and is inherited by every request below. ### 1\. Reach the device The web server listens on the device itself. Replace `{{your-vionyx-ip}}` with the camera's IP and confirm reachability: ```bash curl 'https://{{your-vionyx-ip}}/v1/api/health' # → { "code": 200, "message": "OK", "data": { "status": "ok" } }``` ### 2\. First-time setup A brand-new device has no admin password yet. Check setup status, then set the initial password. ```bash curl 'https://{{your-vionyx-ip}}/v1/api/auth/setup-status' # → { "data": { "completed": false } } curl -X POST 'https://{{your-vionyx-ip}}/v1/api/auth/setup' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "userid": "admin", "password": "ChangeMe123!" }'``` ### 3\. Log in Exchange credentials for a JWT access token (short-lived) and refresh token (long-lived). ```bash curl -X POST 'https://{{your-vionyx-ip}}/v1/api/auth/login' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "userid": "admin", "password": "ChangeMe123!" }' # Response (truncated) # { # "code": 200, "message": "OK", # "data": { # "access_token": "eyJhbGciOi...", # "refresh_token": "eyJhbGciOi...", # "expires_in": 600, # "role": "ADMINISTRATOR" # } # }``` ### 4\. Call an authenticated endpoint Send the access token in `Authorization: Bearer ` on every protected request. ```bash curl 'https://{{your-vionyx-ip}}/v1/api/system/device' \ -H Authorization: Bearer ``` ### 5\. Refresh before expiry Access tokens are short-lived (\~10 minutes). Use the refresh token to mint a new pair — the old refresh token is invalidated immediately. ```bash curl -X POST 'https://{{your-vionyx-ip}}/v1/api/auth/refresh-token' \ -H Authorization: Bearer ;``` AI CAM WebServer REST API specification. --- ​ ## Authentication Every protected endpoint requires a JWT in the `Authorization: Bearer` header. Tokens are issued by `POST /auth/login` and rotated by `POST /auth/refresh-token`. ### Token lifetimes - **Access token** — 10 minutes by default in release builds (3 minutes in debug builds). Short-lived; carry on every request. - **Refresh token** — 1 hour by default in release builds (10 minutes in debug builds). Used only against `/auth/access-token` and `/auth/refresh-token`. Deployments can override these defaults with `ACCESS_TOKEN_DURATION` and `REFRESH_TOKEN_DURATION`. ### Session invalidation Every account has a `session_version`. The following events bump it (and therefore kill every existing token for that account): - Successful login (replaces the previous session) - Logout - Refresh-token rotation - Password change - Admin kicking the account ### Roles - `ADMINISTRATOR` — full access, can manage members. - `OPERATOR` / `VIEWER` — limited writes; depends on per-scope permissions. Endpoints requiring an admin role will respond `403 { "code": 40300, "data": { "reason": "PERMISSION_DENIED" } }`. ### Lock-out Five consecutive failed logins from the same IP × account lock the pair out. Lockout duration grows by 10 minutes per repeated cycle (10, 20, 30 …). A successful login clears the failure counter. --- ## Conventions ### Response envelope Every JSON response — success or error — follows the same envelope: ``` { "code": 200, "message": "OK", "data": }``` The HTTP status mirrors `code` for the common cases. Some endpoints use a finer-grained sub-code in `code` while keeping a stock HTTP status — see Error codes. ### Input validation - **safestring** — text fields reject `<` `>` `"` `'` `;` `|` `` ` ``. - **password** — minimum 8 characters. - **userid** — `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$`. ### Rate limiting - **Login** — 5/minute. Excess attempts block the IP × account pair for 5 minutes × lock-count. - **Sensitive** (config writes, account management) — 60/minute. 1-minute cooldown on overflow. - **General** (any authenticated call) — 120/minute. 1-minute cooldown. Response header: `X-RateLimit-Remaining`. ### Security response headers Every response carries the common headers: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`. UI/HTML responses additionally carry: `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; …`, `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Permissions-Policy: camera=(self), microphone=(), geolocation=(), usb=(), payment=()`. ### PATCH content-types (users) - `application/merge-patch+json` — RFC 7386 (send only changed fields). - `application/json-patch+json` — RFC 6902 (array of op/path/value). --- ## Error codes Errors return the same envelope as success. `code` follows the table below; HTTP status reflects the HTTP semantics. | Code | Reason | HTTP | | :---: | --- | --- | | 40000 | `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` | 400 | | 40100 | `TOKEN_EXPIRED` | 401 | | 40101 | `SESSION_REPLACED` | 401 | | 40102 | `TOKEN_INVALID` | 401 | | 40103 | `SESSION_KICKED` | 401 | | 40300 | `FORBIDDEN` (incl. `PERMISSION_DENIED`) | 403 | | 42900 | `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | 429 | | 42901 | `ACCOUNT_LOCKED` | 429 | | 50300 | `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | ## User CUD sub-codes (90xxx) For user create/update/delete, the body `code` uses a finer-grained catalog that surfaces actionable reasons: | Code | Description | | :---: | --- | | 90101 | Recognition engine busy — retry later | | 90102 | Recognition engine response timed out | | 90103 | Request cancelled by client | | 90201 | Enrollment image empty | | 90202 | Invalid image data | | 90203 | Invalid image source | | 90204 | Face pose rejected | | 90205 | Face quality rejected | | 90206 | Duplicate face | | 90208 | Face template generation failed | | 90209 | Recognition engine busy (NPU lock) | | 90210 | Face not found | | 90301 | Database error | | 90302 | Recognition engine unavailable | | 90399 | Internal error | --- ## Recipes End-to-end flows that span multiple endpoints. Copy, paste, replace placeholders. ### Full login → call → refresh → logout ```bash # 1) Login ACCESS=$(curl -s -X POST 'https://{{your-vionyx-ip}}/v1/api/auth/login' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "userid":"admin", "password":"ChangeMe123!" }' \ | jq -r .data.access_token) REFRESH=$(curl -s -X POST 'https://{{your-vionyx-ip}}/v1/api/auth/login' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "userid":"admin", "password":"ChangeMe123!" }' \ | jq -r .data.refresh_token) # 2) Use the access token curl 'https://{{your-vionyx-ip}}/v1/api/system/device' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS" # 3) Refresh when the access token nears expiry ACCESS=$(curl -s -X POST 'https://{{your-vionyx-ip}}/v1/api/auth/refresh-token' \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $REFRESH" \ | jq -r .data.access_token) # 4) Logout (kills every token bound to this session) curl -X POST 'https://{{your-vionyx-ip}}/v1/api/auth/logout' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS"``` ### Create a user with a face image Embed the face image as base64 in the create request — the server enrolls it atomically. **Face-enrollment consent must be granted in the device admin UI** before any request with a face image succeeds; otherwise the request returns 403. ```bash # 1) Encode the face image B64=$(base64 -i face.jpg | tr -d '\n') # 2) Create the user with the face attached curl -X POST 'https://{{your-vionyx-ip}}/v1/api/users' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "{ \"user_id\": \"emp-1042\", \"user_name\": \"Alice\", \"faces\": [{ \"image_base64\": \"$B64\" }] }" # 3) Verify curl 'https://{{your-vionyx-ip}}/v1/api/users/emp-1042' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" curl 'https://{{your-vionyx-ip}}/v1/api/users/emp-1042/faces' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"``` ### Receive AI events **Pull** — `GET /ai-events/count` + `GET /system/logs?category=AI_EVENT` for historical queries (filter by `type_name`, `user_id`, timestamps). ```bash curl 'https://{{your-vionyx-ip}}/v1/api/ai-events/count' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' curl 'https://{{your-vionyx-ip}}/v1/api/system/logs?category=AI_EVENT&limit=50&type_name=CAM_AI_INTRUSION_ENTRY_AREA_APPEARED' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'``` --- ## API Stability Levels Each endpoint carries a stability badge describing our support commitment. - **stable** (badge "stable") — Supported. We keep it backward-compatible and change it only with care. - **beta** (badge "beta") — Subject to change: available and usable, but we may modify, add, or remove features, fields, or access at our sole discretion. Do not depend on it for long-lived integrations. - **internal** — Used only by the bundled frontend; no support commitment. Internal endpoints are excluded from the public API documentation. The public API documentation lists only **stable** and **beta** endpoints.

item.name: Authentication

request.description:
Log in to obtain a JWT token.
Logging in increments `session_version`, which invalidates all previously issued tokens.

**Login failure lockout policy:**
- The account is temporarily locked after 5 failed login attempts.
- Lockout duration: 5 minutes × lockout count (increases progressively)
  - 1st lockout: 5 minutes, 2nd: 10 minutes, 3rd: 15 minutes, ...
- Lockout applies to the IP + account ID combination.
- The failure count and lockout count reset on a successful login.

**Token validity period:**
- Access Token default: 10 minutes (Release), 3 minutes (Debug)
- Refresh Token default: 1 hour (Release), 10 minutes (Debug)
- Override with `ACCESS_TOKEN_DURATION` and `REFRESH_TOKEN_DURATION` in the deployment environment.

**Password change recommendation:**
- When 90 days have passed since the last password change, the response includes `password_change_recommended: true`.
- The response also provides `password_last_changed_at` (last change timestamp) and `last_login_at` (previous login timestamp).

item.description:
> Rule API for automatically executing a Relay, Audio, or Webhook action based on AI events and user authentication results.
>
> Last updated: 2026-07-15

## 1. General

### Base URL and authentication

```text
https://{device-host}/v1/api
```

All APIs require JWT Bearer authentication. Creating, updating, or deleting a rule, and changing its selected users, requires `rules` edit permission.

```http
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
Content-Type: application/json
```

See the [Authentication](vionyx#authentication) section for how to obtain a token.

### Response

```json
{
  "code": 200,
  "message": "OK",
  "data": null
}
```

### Prerequisite lookups

Before creating a rule, look up the following resources.

| Purpose | API |
| --- | --- |
| Get `ai_event_id` and area/line IDs | `GET /v1/api/ai-events` (see reference §AI Events) |
| Get `relay_port_id` and its usage | `GET /v1/api/relay-ports` |
| Get the `user_id` to select | `GET /v1/api/users` (see reference §People) |
| Get the Relay duration limit | `rule.relay.duration` from `GET /v1/api/capabilities` |

## 2. Endpoints

| Method | Path | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| POST | `/v1/api/rules` | Create a rule |
| GET | `/v1/api/rules` | Get the rule list |
| GET | `/v1/api/rules/{rule_id}` | Get a single rule |
| PUT | `/v1/api/rules/{rule_id}` | Fully update a rule |
| PATCH | `/v1/api/rules/{rule_id}` | Partially update a rule |
| DELETE | `/v1/api/rules/{rule_id}` | Delete a rule |
| GET | `/v1/api/rules/{rule_id}/users` | Get the selected user list |
| POST | `/v1/api/rules/{rule_id}/users` | Add selected users |
| POST | `/v1/api/rules/{rule_id}/users/batch-delete` | Batch-remove selected users |
| DELETE | `/v1/api/rules/{rule_id}/users/{user_id}` | Remove a single selected user |
| GET | `/v1/api/relay-ports` | Get relay ports and their rule usage |

`GET /v1/api/rules/simples` does not fully represent a Relay Rule's branched actions, so do not use it for Relay integrations.

## 3. Identifying Relay Rules and the execution model

A rule is treated as a Relay Rule when its body includes `users`.

| Type | `users` | Action type | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Relay Rule | Present | `authenticated`/`unauthenticated` branches | Execute a different action depending on the authentication result |
| Regular Rule | Absent | Top-level `config`/`schedule` | An action with no authentication result involved |

A Relay Rule's action executes only after passing all three of the following switches.

1. The rule's `enable`
2. The action's `enable`
3. The selected branch's `enable`

### Authentication result matching

| `users.mode` | `authenticated` branch | `unauthenticated` branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ALL` | Registered and authenticated users | Unauthenticated users, or users not registered |
| `SELECTED` | Authenticated users on the selected list | Unauthenticated users, and authenticated users not on the selected list |

If looking up the selected list for a `SELECTED` rule fails and a safe determination cannot be made, that Relay Rule does not execute.

A `SELECTED` rule with zero selected users and `auto_add_new_users=false` is treated as a subjectless rule. All input is then processed through the `unauthenticated` branch, so enable that branch when using this type.

### Supported AI event conditions

| `ai_event_type` | Matching ID field | Execution input |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FACE_MOVEMENT_TRACKING` | Entry/exit: `entry_area_ids` · Face authentication: `face_areas` of the linked AI event | Face authentication, area entry/exit |
| `INTRUSION` | `intrusion_area_ids` | Entering/leaving an intrusion area |
| `LINE_CROSSING` | `crossing_line_ids` | Line crossing |
| `PEOPLE_COUNTING` | `counting_area_ids` | People count change, or reaching the people-count limit |

Face authentication input is matched against **the `face_areas` of the linked AI event's setting**, not the rule's `entry_area_ids` (if `face_areas` is empty, it matches regardless of area). At least one ID is required in the array corresponding to the condition type. As an exception, a face-authentication-only rule with `FACE_MOVEMENT_TRACKING`, `face_recognition=true`, and `entry_area=false` can omit `entry_area_ids`.

### Caution: duplicate execution

If the same person passes face authentication and then enters an area, both the face authentication and the area entry can each trigger an action. The server does not automatically merge these two inputs. If an action must run only once, configure the AI event's toggles and the rule's condition so that only one kind of input is generated.

## 4. Data model

### Rule

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rule_id` | integer | Response only | Rule ID issued by the server |
| `name` | string | Y | Rule name, up to 255 characters |
| `enable` | boolean | Y | Whether the rule is enabled |
| `users` | object | Y | Relay Rule discriminator and user selection policy |
| `condition` | object | Y | AI event condition |
| `actions` | array | Y | List of branched actions |

### users

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | string | Y | `ALL` or `SELECTED` |
| `auto_add_new_users` | boolean | N | Automatically adds users who later enroll a face to the selected list. Always normalized to `true` when `mode` is `ALL` |
| `user_ids` | string[] | N | Initial selected-user list, used only in the create request |
| `selected_count` | integer | Response only | Current number of selected users |

`users.user_ids` in a `PUT` or `PATCH` body does not change the selected list. After creation, manage the selected list through the `/rules/{rule_id}/users` sub-resource.

**Condition**

```json
{
  "condition_type": "AI_EVENT",
  "config": {
    "ai_event_id": 1,
    "ai_event_type": "FACE_MOVEMENT_TRACKING",
    "entry_area_ids": [1],
    "event_type": {
      "face_recognition": true,
      "entry_area": true
    }
  }
}
```

The toggles available in `event_type` are `face_recognition`, `entry_area`, `intrusion_area`, `crossing_line`, and `counting_area`. The rule executes only if the corresponding input is enabled in the actual AI event setting.

**Branched action**

```json
{
  "action_type": "RELAY",
  "enable": true,
  "authenticated": {
    "enable": true,
    "config": {
      "relay_port_id": "RelayOutputToken_1",
      "duration": 3
    },
    "schedule": { "always": true }
  },
  "unauthenticated": {
    "enable": false
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action_type` | string | Y | `RELAY`, `AUDIO`, `WEBHOOK` |
| `enable` | boolean | Y | Action master switch |
| `authenticated` | object | N | Authenticated branch |
| `unauthenticated` | object | N | Unauthenticated branch |
| `authenticated.enable` | boolean | Y if the branch exists | Whether the authenticated branch is enabled |
| `unauthenticated.enable` | boolean | Y if the branch exists | Whether the unauthenticated branch is enabled |
| `config` | object | Y for an active branch | Per-action settings |
| `schedule` | object | N | If omitted, an active branch is normalized to `{ "always": true }` |

The current Relay Rule runtime executes only an active branch's `schedule.always=true`. Schedule execution based on `schedule_id` is not supported, so use `always=true` for external integrations.

### RELAY config

| Field | Type | Required | Constraint |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `relay_port_id` | string | Y | A port returned by `GET /relay-ports` |
| `duration` | integer | Y | In seconds. See `rule.relay.duration` in capabilities for the limit, currently `1..120` |

Multiple rules can share the same `relay_port_id`. If multiple rules trigger on the same port at overlapping times, the relay's open duration is overwritten by the `duration` of the most recently accepted open command (the timer resets). Check `used_by` in `GET /relay-ports` to see which rules are using which ports.

## 5. Creating a Relay Rule

```http
POST /v1/api/rules
```

The following example opens the relay for 3 seconds when a selected user enters the area, and plays an audio announcement for all other users.

```json
{
  "name": "Main entrance access",
  "enable": true,
  "users": {
    "mode": "SELECTED",
    "auto_add_new_users": false,
    "user_ids": ["vip-user-1", "vip-user-2"]
  },
  "condition": {
    "condition_type": "AI_EVENT",
    "config": {
      "ai_event_id": 1,
      "ai_event_type": "FACE_MOVEMENT_TRACKING",
      "entry_area_ids": [1],
      "event_type": {
        "face_recognition": true,
        "entry_area": true
      }
    }
  },
  "actions": [
    {
      "action_type": "RELAY",
      "enable": true,
      "authenticated": {
        "enable": true,
        "config": {
          "relay_port_id": "RelayOutputToken_1",
          "duration": 3
        },
        "schedule": { "always": true }
      },
      "unauthenticated": {
        "enable": false
      }
    },
    {
      "action_type": "AUDIO",
      "enable": true,
      "authenticated": {
        "enable": false
      },
      "unauthenticated": {
        "enable": true,
        "config": {
          "audio_clip_id": 2,
          "repeat": 1
        },
        "schedule": { "always": true }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
  "message": "OK",

        "ai_event_id": 1,

```

## 6. Executing Relay when the people-count limit is reached

Reaching the people-count limit is not an event tied to a specific user, so a regular rule that doesn't use `users` or authentication branches is recommended. A top-level `RELAY` action is allowed only for the `PEOPLE_COUNTING` condition.

```json
{
  "name": "Count limit siren",
  "enable": true,
  "condition": {
    "condition_type": "AI_EVENT",
    "config": {
      "ai_event_id": 2,
      "ai_event_type": "PEOPLE_COUNTING",
      "counting_area_ids": [9]
    }
  },
  "actions": [
    {
      "action_type": "RELAY",
      "config": {
        "relay_port_id": "RelayOutputToken_1",
        "duration": 10
      },
      "schedule": { "always": true }
    }
  ]
}
```

A top-level `RELAY` triggers on **both** a people-count change (4104) and the people-count limit being reached (4105).
To react only to the limit being reached, restrict the input itself by setting the linked AI event's People Counting condition to `COUNT_LIMIT`.

A Relay Rule with users linked can react to a people-count change input, but does not react to the people-count-limit-reached input. A subjectless Relay Rule with 0 `SELECTED` users can also be used, but the regular rule form above is recommended in this case to avoid confusion between the two branches.

## 7. Get, update, and delete

### Get list

```http
GET /v1/api/rules?offset=0&limit=100&ai_event_type=FACE_MOVEMENT_TRACKING
```

| Query | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `offset` | `0` | Starting position |
| `limit` | `1000` | Number of results to return, max 1000 |
| `ai_event_type` | None | AI event type filter |

The response `data` is an array of rules. Whether `users` is present on each item distinguishes a Relay Rule.

### Get a single rule

```http
GET /v1/api/rules/10
```

The response's `condition.config.ai_event` may include information about the linked AI event.

### Full and partial update

```http
PUT /v1/api/rules/10
PATCH /v1/api/rules/10
```

`PUT` takes the entire rule body; `PATCH` takes only the fields to change. Neither API changes the selected-user list, so use the user sub-resource below for that.

### Delete

```http
DELETE /v1/api/rules/10
```

Deleting a rule also deletes its selected-user associations and removes it from `used_by` in `relay-ports`. Deleting a rule that does not exist is not a failure — it is an idempotent operation that succeeds with `code=204` (HTTP 200).

## 8. Managing selected users

The selected-users API allows adding and removing users only on a Relay Rule with `users.mode=SELECTED`. A user to select must exist and have at least one enrolled face.

### List

```http
GET /v1/api/rules/10/users?offset=0&limit=50
```

```json
{
  "code": 200,
  "message": "OK",
  "data": {
    "rule_id": 10,
    "mode": "SELECTED",
    "total": 2,
    "items": [
      { "user_id": "vip-user-1", "user_name": "Visitor One" },
      { "user_id": "vip-user-2", "user_name": "Visitor Two" }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Add

```http
POST /v1/api/rules/10/users
```

```json
{ "user_ids": ["vip-user-3", "vip-user-4"] }
```

```json
{ "code": 200, "message": "OK", "data": { "added": 2, "total": 4 } }
```

A user that is already selected is not added again.

### Batch remove

```http
POST /v1/api/rules/10/users/batch-delete
```

```json
{ "user_ids": ["vip-user-3"] }
```

```json
{ "code": 200, "message": "OK", "data": { "removed": 1, "total": 3 } }
```

### Remove a single user

```http
DELETE /v1/api/rules/10/users/vip-user-3
```

Removing a user not on the list also succeeds, with `removed=0`.

## 9. Get relay ports

```http
GET /v1/api/relay-ports
```

```json
{
  "code": 200,
  "message": "OK",
  "data": {
    "ports": [
      {
        "relay_port_id": "RelayOutputToken_1",
        "label": "RelayOutputToken_1",
        "source": "DEVICE",
        "available": true,
        "used_by": [
          { "rule_id": 10, "name": "Main entrance access" },
          { "rule_id": 12, "name": "Intrusion alarm" }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

`used_by` is the full list of rules using the port; an unused port shows an empty array `[]`. A port already in use can still be selected in a new rule — if multiple rules share one port, the open duration is overwritten by the `duration` of the most recently accepted open command. `available=false` means the port cannot currently operate.

## 10. Error codes

| HTTP | Body `code` | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | 400 | Request format or semantic validation failed |
| 400 | 90403 | `user_id` does not exist |
| 400 | 90404 | User has no enrolled face |
| 400 | 90405 | No executable action exists |
| 404 | 404 | Rule does not exist — GET/PUT/PATCH/selected-users APIs. `DELETE` returns idempotent success with `code=204` instead of 404 |
| 409 | 409 | Selected-users API called on a rule that is not `SELECTED` |
| 409 | 90401 | Maximum number of rules exceeded |
| 500 | 500 | Internal server error |

Error example:

```json
{
  "code": 90403,
  "message": "unknown user_id: vip-user-9",
  "data": null
}
```

`message` is a human-readable string with no fixed format. Branch program logic on `code` instead.

item.description:
> REST API for directly querying and controlling relay outputs from an external system.
>
> Last updated: 2026-07-15

## 1. General

### Base URL

```text
https://{device-host}/v1/api
```

All requests use HTTPS and JWT Bearer authentication.

```http
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
Content-Type: application/json
```

See the [Authentication](vionyx#authentication) section for how to obtain a token.

### Permissions

| Account role | Allowed APIs |
| --- | --- |
| `USER` | `GET /relay-ports` |
| `OPERATOR`, `ADMINISTRATOR` | Port lookup, state lookup, all control APIs |

### Response

Success and failure responses use a common envelope.

```json
{
  "code": 200,
  "message": "OK",
  "data": null
}
```

`code` generally matches the HTTP status, but some relay errors use a 5-digit code to distinguish the cause.

## 2. Endpoints

| Method | Path | Minimum permission | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/v1/api/relay-ports` | `USER` | Get relay ports and their rule usage |
| GET | `/v1/api/relay/state?relay_port_id={id}` | `OPERATOR` | Get the current relay state |
| POST | `/v1/api/relay/open` | `OPERATOR` | Open temporarily for a given duration |
| POST | `/v1/api/relay/lock` | `OPERATOR` | Fixed lock |
| POST | `/v1/api/relay/unlock` | `OPERATOR` | Fixed unlock |
| POST | `/v1/api/relay/release` | `OPERATOR` | Release fixed control |

## 3. Get relay ports

```http
GET /v1/api/relay-ports
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "code": 200,
  "message": "OK",
  "data": {
    "ports": [
      {
        "relay_port_id": "RelayOutputToken_1",
        "label": "RelayOutputToken_1",
        "source": "DEVICE",
        "available": true,
        "used_by": [ { "rule_id": 10, "name": "Main entrance access" } ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `relay_port_id` | string | Port identifier used for state queries and control requests |
| `label` | string | Display name |
| `source` | string | Port origin. Currently always `DEVICE` |
| `available` | boolean | Whether the port is currently controllable |
| `slave_osdp_id` | integer | OSDP ID when this is a slave port. Omitted otherwise |
| `used_by` | array | List of rules using the port (`rule_id`·`name`, sorted by `rule_id` ascending). Empty array `[]` if unused |

`used_by` shows the port's rule usage. Multiple rules can share one port, and a direct control API call is also possible on a port that is already in use. While fixed control is active on a port, automatic rule actions on that port are suppressed.

## 4. Get state

```http
GET /v1/api/relay/state?relay_port_id=RelayOutputToken_1
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "code": 200,
  "message": "OK",
  "data": {
    "relay_port_id": "RelayOutputToken_1",
    "current_state": "CLOSE",
    "control_mode": "IDLE"
  }
}
```

| `control_mode` | `current_state` | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `IDLE` | `CLOSE` | Default state with no active control |
| `TIMED_OPEN` | `OPEN` | A temporary open duration is in progress |
| `FIXED_LOCK` | `CLOSE` | Fixed lock until `release` |
| `FIXED_UNLOCK` | `OPEN` | Fixed unlock until `release` |

## 5. Temporary open

```http
POST /v1/api/relay/open
```

```json
{
  "relay_port_id": "RelayOutputToken_1",
  "duration": 3
}
```

| Field | Type | Required | Constraint |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `relay_port_id` | string | Y | Identifier returned by `GET /relay-ports` |
| `duration` | integer | Y | `1..120`, in seconds |

Success response:

```json
{
  "code": 200,
  "message": "OK",
  "data": {
    "relay_port_id": "RelayOutputToken_1",
    "current_state": "OPEN",
    "control_mode": "TIMED_OPEN"
  }
}
```

When the duration ends, the state returns to `CLOSE`/`IDLE`. Calling this again during `TIMED_OPEN` resets the existing timer with the new `duration`. Rejected with `40900` during fixed lock or fixed unlock.

## 6. Fixed lock

```http
POST /v1/api/relay/lock
```

```json
{
  "relay_port_id": "RelayOutputToken_1"
}
```

On success, `current_state` is `CLOSE` and `control_mode` is `FIXED_LOCK`.

## 7. Fixed unlock

```http
POST /v1/api/relay/unlock
```

```json
{
  "relay_port_id": "RelayOutputToken_1"
}
```

On success, `current_state` is `OPEN` and `control_mode` is `FIXED_UNLOCK`.

You can switch directly between `FIXED_LOCK` and `FIXED_UNLOCK` without calling `release`; the later request takes precedence.

## 8. Release fixed control

```http
POST /v1/api/relay/release
```

```json
{
  "relay_port_id": "RelayOutputToken_1"
}
```

Success response:

```json
{
  "code": 200,
  "message": "OK",
  "data": {
    "relay_port_id": "RelayOutputToken_1",
    "current_state": "CLOSE",
    "control_mode": "IDLE"
  }
}
```

Calling this on a port that is already `IDLE` also succeeds, so it can be used idempotently.

## 9. Control conflict rules

| Current state | New request | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `IDLE` | Any control | Request applied |
| `TIMED_OPEN` | `open` | Timer reset |
| `TIMED_OPEN` | `lock`/`unlock` | Timer canceled and fixed control applied |
| `FIXED_LOCK`/`FIXED_UNLOCK` | `open` | HTTP 409, `code=40900` |
| `FIXED_LOCK` | `unlock` | Switches to fixed unlock |
| `FIXED_UNLOCK` | `lock` | Switches to fixed lock |
| Any state | `release` | Switches to `IDLE` |

While fixed control is active, an automatic rule's temporary-open request is not applied. Automatic rule actions are allowed again after `release`.

## 10. Error responses

`data.reason` in an error response is a stable identifier suitable for program branching.
`message` is a reference string passed through as-is from the device and **its value is not fixed** — always branch on `code` and `data.reason`.

```json
{
  "code": 40900,
  "message": "door locked",
  "data": {
    "reason": "CONTROL_LEVEL_TOO_LOW"
  }
}
```

| HTTP | body `code` | `data.reason` | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | 400 | `VALIDATION` | JSON format or type error |
| 400 | 40002 | `INVALID_DURATION` | `duration` missing or out of range |
| 401 | 40102, etc. | `TOKEN_INVALID`, etc. | Token missing, invalid, or expired |
| 403 | 40300 | `FORBIDDEN` or `PERMISSION_DENIED` | Insufficient permission |
| 404 | 40400 | `RELAY_PORT_NOT_FOUND` | Port ID missing or does not exist |
| 409 | 40900 | `CONTROL_LEVEL_TOO_LOW` | Conflicts with fixed control |
| 409 | 40901 | `RELAY_PORT_UNAVAILABLE` | Port unavailable |
| 500 | 500 | `INTERNAL` | The device judged the request invalid — since the request passed server-side pre-validation, report this as a defect |
| 503 | 50300 | `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` | Device not responding, or control failed |

## 11. Retry guidance

- `GET /relay/state` and `POST /relay/release` can be retried safely.
- Retrying `POST /relay/open` restarts the open timer.
- `POST /relay/lock` and `/unlock` can request the same state again, but may overwrite another caller's most recent request.
- If a control request returns `503`, the actual device state may be unclear — check the current state with `GET /relay/state` before blindly resending.

## 12. Related documents

- To automatically trigger a relay based on rule conditions, see the [Relay Rule guide](vionyx?api=ai-eventrule-settings).
- For obtaining an authentication token, see the [Authentication](vionyx#authentication) section.

Switches the tunnel mode or updates the current mode's settings. The schema of `setting` is determined by the `mode` value in the same request (same discriminator as GET). Follows PATCH semantics, where only the sent fields are updated. Include `cloudflare_api_token` only when changing it; if omitted, the BE-stored value is retained.

The WebServer Tunnel and the CLUe Tunnel (`features.tunnel` in `/v1/api/integration/3rd/clue`) operate independently and can both be enabled at the same time — each spawns its own separate cloudflared child process in an isolated working directory, so there is no PID/CNAME/tunnel resource conflict.

bodyFields.name: mode
bodyFields.description:
Operation mode of the WebServer Tunnel. Role as the discriminator for the `oneOf` setting.

- `OFF`: Disabled. No external exposure.  
- `CF_QUICK`: The WebServer spawns cloudflared itself. `*.trycloudflare.com` is the temporary URL.  
- `CF_NAMED`: The WebServer calls the Cloudflare API with user credentials to create a permanent Tunnel + DNS CNAME and spawn cloudflared. Credentials must be entered in the setting.  
- `CF_NAMED_TOKEN`: The user directly creates a named tunnel on the Cloudflare dashboard and enters only the connector token. The WebServer does not call the Cloudflare API and spawns only cloudflared using the token. When cloudflared is executed, `--url http://127.0.0.1:81` is also passed to enforce internal routing. As an additional guard, if the ingress's `service` is not `http://127.0.0.1:81` or `http://localhost:81`, the tunnel is not opened and terminated immediately. The external URL is the first hostname in the ingress configuration log.

Turning the CLUe Tunnel itself on and off is a toggle of `features.tunnel` in `/v1/api/integration/3rd/clue` and is not represented by the value of this enum. The WebServer Tunnel and CLUe Tunnel operate independently and can be turned on simultaneously — since each spawns a separate cloudflared child in an isolated working directory, there are no PID / CNAME / Tunnel resource conflicts.

item.name: Cert

request.description:
Returns the device's Root CA certificate in PEM format. Clients import this file into the OS/browser trust root store so they can trust the HTTPS/RTSPS certificates issued by the device.

**Authentication not required (public)**: the certificate itself is public information (already exposed during the TLS handshake), and a client connecting for the first time is at a stage before obtaining a token — requiring authentication would make bootstrapping the trust chain impossible.

**Response body**: a PEM-encoded X.509 certificate. The private key is never included.

Returns 404 if the file has not yet been generated (before EnsureRootCA runs, right after boot).

header.description:
Filename derived from the cert's Subject CN —
`Suprema_ViOnyx_Device_<SN>_Root_CA.crt` when device SN is
known, falling back to `Suprema_ViOnyx_Device_Root_CA.crt`.
Lets clients managing multiple devices keep imports distinct.

item.description: Device PKI — the Root CA download endpoint. Provides a PEM certificate for import into the OS/browser trust store so clients can trust the device.
